summary: Researched the evening before (Fri 13 Nov), so no lineups are out yet; the morning check and the pre-kickoff check re-test the picks. Saturday of the international break: 16 candidates (four Nations League games, two NHL games, a LoL Worlds playoff and nine UFC 334 fights). The four best-covered games, all Nations League, were researched first and all four are kept at medium. Norway over Wales (p 0.77; Haaland and Odegaard expected, both sides must win, but Norway have lost 3 of 4 group games and Wales won the last three meetings). Portugal over Denmark (p 0.63; Portugal 4 from 4, but already through, missing Cancelo, Conceicao and Mendes; Denmark score in most games). Sweden over Bosnia (p 0.62; a win clinches the group, Gyokeres, Isak and Kulusevski fit; Bosnia unbeaten in the group and drew 1-1 in October). Austria over Ireland (p 0.575, draw 0.26, so only double chance or draw no bet; Austria missing several regulars, no clean sheet in 8, 2-2 in Dublin in October; no Elo rating found). The other 12 (NHL, LoL, UFC) were not researched because the four kept games already make a medium slip.

checks.team_news: Norway: Jorgen Strand Larsen withdrew injured and Fredrik Aursnes withdrew on 8 Nov (TNT Sports, Sports Mole). Alexander Sorloth is back after a muscle injury, Heggem should be available, Haaland expected to win his 60th cap. Four Norway players are one booking from suspension, including Odegaard. Wales: Ben Cabango and Sorba Thomas suspended, Kieffer Moore withdrew (Aaron Collins called up), Jordan James not in squad. Joe Rodon is back from a hamstring injury and Harry Wilson is available for the first time since March. No major injury concerns reported beyond that.
checks.lineups: Lineups are not out (evening before). Sports Mole predicted Norway: Selvik; Ryerson, Ajer, Ostigard, Wolfe; Odegaard, Berge, Berg; Bobb, Haaland, Nusa. Predicted Wales: Ward; N Williams, Mepham, Davies, Dasilva; Ampadu, R Colwill; Johnson, Cullen, Wilson; D James. TNT Sports lists Ryerson as likely right-back for Norway. Both sources predict Haaland starting. No rotation reported.
checks.rotation: Last game: both sides played in the previous window, Norway beat Denmark 3-2 and lost 1-2 away to Portugal, Wales lost 0-2 and 0-1 to Denmark and 0-1 to Portugal. Next game for both is on 17 Nov: Norway away at Denmark in Copenhagen, Wales vs Portugal (TNT Sports). The Denmark game is a modest rotation temptation for Norway, but Solbakken says they must beat Wales and the group stakes are high, so heavy rotation is unlikely. Norway play at home, Wales travel.
checks.motivation: Group A4 is tight. Per Sports Mole and beIN Sports, Norway have 3 points from 4 games (1 win, 3 defeats) and must beat Wales to keep quarter-final hopes alive, and also need to beat Denmark. Wales are level on 3 points and a win lifts them to 6, so both sides need the win and Wales will go all in (Solbakken: it is like a boxing match, going fist to fist). Both teams have strong motivation, which raises the draw and upset risk compared with a one-sided fixture.
checks.form: Norway last five (TNT Sports): L W L L L, 7 goals scored and 10 conceded. Nations League: W 3-2 Denmark, L 1-2 Portugal, L 1-2 Wales, L 1-2 Portugal. Wales last five: L L L W L, 3 scored and 7 conceded. Nations League: L 0-1 Portugal, L 0-2 Denmark, W 2-1 Norway, L 0-1 Denmark. Norway's form is poor for a heavy favourite, with three defeats from four. No xG found.
checks.h2h: Wales beat Norway 2-1 in Cardiff on 1 Oct 2026 (Dan James, Neco Williams) and have won the last three meetings. Overall 12 meetings, four wins each and four draws (Sports Mole). Wales are a low-block, counter-attacking side that lost narrowly to the top sides, and Norway have conceded in each of their four group games. Match-ups in this group tend to be tight and goals come mostly from Haaland.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/soccer/uefa.nations/scoreboard?dates=20261114): Norway 1.21, draw 6.50, Wales 10.00, total 3.5. Opening was 1.22 / 5.75 / 8.50, so the draw and Wales price drifted out slightly and Norway barely moved. De-vigged 76.5% / 14.2% / 9.3%. TNT Sports (12 Nov): BTTS yes 1.83, under 3.5 goals 1.73, Norway 2-1 correct score 9.00. Polymarket 24h move for Norway: 0.795 to 0.795, no change. Polymarket 79.4 / 13.3 / 7.4 is about 3 points above the de-vigged DraftKings price on Norway, so I shade Norway down slightly.
checks.models: World Football Elo (https://www.eloratings.net/): Norway 1901, Wales 1681, a gap of 220 giving an expected score of 0.863 for Norway with a draw counted as half. That is consistent with a win probability near 0.75-0.78 once draws are separated out. Previews from Sports Mole and The Hard Tackle both pick Norway 2-1, i.e. a win by one goal, which is not strongly supportive of the -1.5 handicap.
checks.venue_weather: Ullevaal Stadion, Oslo, Norway's regular home ground, grass, kick-off 17:00 UTC. yr.no forecast: partly cloudy, no precipitation, light wind, high about 5C and low about 0C. No pitch problems reported and nothing unusual about the venue.

games.reason: Norway are a clear favourite at home, with Elo 1901 against 1681 and a 3-point lead in market price over the book, and both sides must win, so Norway should keep their strongest XI with Haaland, Odegaard and Nusa. No hard exclusion applies: fixture verified, no confirmed rotation, not a derby, no coach changes found, normal venue and mild weather. I put the draw at 15% (above the 13% Polymarket price) because both teams are playing for the result, Wales have won the last three meetings including 2-1 in October, and Norway have lost three of their last four. That is above the 10-15% usual for this kind of favourite but still under 25%, so a straight win is allowed; the confidence is medium rather than high.
games.main_risk: Draw or another Wales upset: Wales beat Norway 2-1 in October and have won the last three meetings, Norway have lost three of their four group games and conceded in every one, Wales need a win and will play all in, and Norway have a Denmark game on 17 Nov. Lineups are unconfirmed and four Norway players, including Odegaard, are one booking from suspension. The handicap -1.5 is weaker because previews pick 2-1.

checks.team_news: Portugal: Joao Cancelo and Francisco Conceicao suspended (Conceicao red card in Porto), Nuno Mendes injured; Rafael Leao and Nuno Tavares also listed injured by Al Jazeera; Joao Palhinha missed Thursday training with flu-like symptoms but trained Friday (Portugoal). Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football (first game without him). Denmark: Patrick Dorgu out (hamstring), Andreas Christensen not called up (fitness); no suspensions but six players one booking from a ban (Sports Mole, Al Jazeera, Portugoal). No bad news on Costa, Dias, Fernandes or Vitinha.
checks.lineups: Not confirmed, predicted only. Portugal (Sports Mole): Costa; Dalot, Dias, Veiga, Nazinho; Vitinha, Fernandes, J Neves; Felix, Ramos, Neto. Portugal (Portugoal/Al Jazeera) similar 4-4-1-1 with Neves/Neto/Felix/Ramos and Costa in goal. Denmark (Sports Mole): Hermansen; Kristensen, Andersen, Provstgaard, Maehle; Isaksen, Hjulmand, Hojbjerg, Daramy; Hojlund, Froholdt. The core is consistent across sources; fullback and wide slots differ.
checks.rotation: Portugal have already secured a quarter-final place and need only a point to win Group A4. Coach Jorge Jesus said he wants to start integrating younger players and seven Portugal players are one yellow from a ban for the Wales game (Portugoal), so some changes are possible, but no heavy rotation has been announced. Denmark fight for the quarter-finals (need four points from two games to be sure) and should be at full strength.
checks.motivation: Portugal: group already won in effect (12 points from 4 wins, quarter-final secured, top spot confirmed with a draw). Denmark: second on 6 points, need a result to secure qualification, so they are more motivated. Slightly lower stakes for Portugal is a soft risk.
checks.form: Portugal won all 4 Nations League group games (W-W-W-W; last five W-W-W-W-L per Al Jazeera). Denmark 2 wins (both vs Wales, including 2-0) and 2 defeats (3-2 vs Norway, 4-2 vs Portugal); last five W-L-W-L-D. Hojlund has 3 of Denmark's 7 goals in the competition. xG not found.
checks.h2h: Portugal beat Denmark 4-2 in Copenhagen on 1 October. All-time: Portugal 13 wins, Denmark 4, 2 draws in 19 meetings (Al Jazeera); Sports Mole says Denmark won only 4 of 19. Denmark will score in most games (predicted 2-1 and 3-1 in previews), so a draw via a goal-for-goal match is the main route.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (data.odds, source https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/soccer/uefa.nations/scoreboard?dates=20261114): Portugal 1.49 / draw 4.50 / Denmark 5.50, de-vigged 62.5% / 20.6% / 16.9%, opening 1.45/4.40/5.25 (home drifted slightly out), total 3.5. A TNT Sports preview shows Portugal 1.50 and Denmark 5.50. Polymarket 65/20/16, 24h move on Portugal flat (0.645 to 0.645). Opta supercomputer (via Al Jazeera): Portugal 59.4%, draw 21.2%, Denmark 19.4%.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net): Portugal 2055, Denmark 1861; expected score for Portugal 0.845 (draw counted as half), consistent with roughly 63% win / 21% draw. Opta supercomputer 59.4/21.2/19.4 is a little more cautious on Portugal.
checks.venue_weather: Estadio Municipal de Braga, Braga, Portugal, Saturday 14 Nov 19:45 local/GMT. Portugal home game at a regular Portugal national-team venue. No weather forecast or pitch problem found in the sources read; unverified, not treated as a risk.

games.reason: Fixture verified (UEFA Nations League Group A4, Portugal vs Denmark, Braga, Sat 14 Nov 19:45 UTC) by Sports Mole, Al Jazeera and Portugoal. No hard exclusion: no confirmed rotation, not a derby, Jorge Jesus has coached all four group games (not a recent change), normal home venue. Portugal are clearly stronger (Elo 2055 vs 1861; bookmaker, Opta and Polymarket agree around 60-65% win, draw about 20-21%) and in form, but they miss Cancelo, Conceicao and Mendes, are playing their first game without Ronaldo and have little at stake. p is set slightly below the market on Portugal. Lineups are not confirmed, so medium rather than high. Draw no bet or double chance are the safer legs; a straight win is allowed at the 21% draw estimate.
games.main_risk: A draw (about 21%) or Denmark upset against a Portugal side that is already qualified, may make changes to integrate younger players and is missing Cancelo, Conceicao and Mendes. Denmark are more motivated and score regularly (Hojlund). Lineups not yet announced.

checks.team_news: Sweden: Potter said all are available after Friday training; Gyokeres, Nygren and Kulusevski sat out Thursday's session but trained Friday (Fotbollskanalen, SVT). Isak reported available. Absent from camp through injury: Starfelt, Hien, Holm, Bergvall; Zeneli withdrew 9 Nov with no replacement (svenskafans/bet365 squad news). Bosnia: Muharemovic suspended, Hadzikadunic out with a calf tear; Dedic back from injury; Dzeko not in squad (retired from internationals) per Goal/Sarajevo Times/Sports Mole snippets. No confirmed rotation news.
checks.lineups: Nothing official yet. Sportsgambler predicted Sweden 4-4-2: Johansson; Beijmo, Lagerbielke, Nilsson Lindelof, Svensson; Elanga, Karlstrom, Ayari, Njie; Isak, Gyokeres. bet365 Sweden also projects Isak and Gyokeres together in a 4-4-2; Fotbollskanalen tips Skoglund at right back (partly dated). Potter does not expect many surprises. Bosnia predicted 3-4-2-1: Zlomislic; Radeljic, Katic, Kolasinac; Dedic, Gigovic, Basic, Memic; Bajraktarevic, Alajbegovic; Demirovic. Some previews still list Dzeko, which conflicts with the retirement reports.
checks.rotation: Sweden's previous competitive game was 5 Oct (3-1 vs Poland per the Wikipedia table as of 5 Oct); next game is Poland away on 17 Nov, so a full week of rest and no travel. Bosnia play Romania at home in Zenica on 17 Nov and travel to Stockholm. Both sides have the same 3-day turnaround to 17 Nov; Sweden have more at stake tomorrow, so no rotation is expected.
checks.motivation: Group B4 before this round: Sweden 10 pts (3W 1D, 7:3), Bosnia 8 (2W 2D, 6:3), Poland 4, Romania 0. A Swedish win gives 13 pts, which Bosnia cannot catch, so Sweden would win the group and go up to League A (Swedish media, Swedenherald). Bosnia need a result to keep the group alive. Both are motivated.
checks.form: Sweden's last five competitive games: W 1-0 at Romania, D 1-1 at Bosnia, W 3-1 v Poland, W 2-1 v Romania, L 0-3 to France (World Cup). Over the last 10: 6W 2D 2L. Bosnia's last five: W 1-0 v Poland, D 1-1 v Sweden, W 4-2 at Romania, D 0-0 at Poland, L 0-2 to USA (World Cup). Over the last 10: 5W 3D 2L. Bosnia are unbeaten in this group, with 2 draws in 4. No xG found.
checks.h2h: The latest meeting, 2 Oct 2026 in Bosnia, ended 1-1 (Sweden reportedly had five sick players that week, per Hurbra headline). Sources disagree on any earlier meetings. Bosnia drew 2 of 4 group games and Sweden 1 of 4, so the draw is the main threat.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN: Sweden 1.50, draw 4.10, Bosnia 5.75 (opened 1.49/4.00/5.50), de-vigged 61.5/22.5/16.0, total 2.5. BetMGM via Sportsgambler: Sweden -213, draw +350, Bosnia +510, AH Sweden -1.25, Over 2.5 -175, BTTS Yes -143. Polymarket (gamma API, tonight): Sweden 0.635, draw 0.215, Bosnia 0.155. 24h move on Sweden 0.625 to 0.635, relative +1.6%, a small shift in Sweden's favour. Sources agree.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net): Sweden 1774 v Bosnia 1672, expected score for Sweden 0.762 with a draw counted as half. That is about 0.62 win after allowing for the draw, in line with the market.
checks.venue_weather: Strawberry Arena, Solna (Stockholm), Sweden's normal home ground, kick-off 20:45 local (19:45 UTC). The roof is closed per the venue's ticket page, so weather and pitch are not a factor. No reliable forecast found; cold evening expected.

games.reason: Fixture verified: Nations League B Group 4, round 5, Sat 14 Nov 2026 at the Strawberry Arena. Sweden are the home favourite on 1774 v 1672 Elo, with a market price of about 61 to 63.5 percent and a clear incentive (a win clinches the group and promotion). There are no key absences, and Gyokeres, Kulusevski and Nygren are fit. Bosnia are missing a suspended centre-back and an injured one, and Dzeko has retired. I put the draw at 23 percent, within the 25 percent limit for a straight win, and p is within 5 points of the market on every outcome. Confidence is medium because Bosnia drew 1-1 in October, are unbeaten in the group and defend well. Double chance or draw no bet is safer than the straight win. No hard exclusion applies: no coach change, no derby, a home venue and a closed roof.
games.main_risk: A draw is the main risk. Bosnia are unbeaten in the group (two draws, including 1-1 against Sweden in October) and have a compact 3-4-2-1 shape. Sweden's squad has depth gaps in defence (Starfelt, Hien and Holm out). The starting XI is unconfirmed, and Gyokeres, Kulusevski and Nygren had a minor training scare on Thursday.

checks.team_news: Austria: RTE (13 Nov) lists Patrick Wimmer, Xaver Schlager and Alexander Prass injured, and David Alaba, Paul Wanner, Carney Chukwuemeka and Marco Grull missing; Mightytips/Racing Post also list Maximilian Wober and Nikolas Veratschnig out; Yusuf Demir and Raul Florucz called up as replacements; Sasa Kalajdzic back in squad per one summary. Sources conflict on whether Prass and X. Schlager are fit. Ireland: no injury concerns in RTE; Nathan Collins and Mark Travers return, Gavin Bazunu out; Joel Bagan, Killian Phillips and Owen Elding left the squad (Racing Post).
checks.lineups: Not out yet. Sports Mole predicted Austria: A Schlager; Posch, Bacher, Danso, Laimer; Seiwald, X Schlager; Florucz, Schmid, Prass; Gregoritsch. Racing Post/Mightytips: 4-2-3-1 with Posch/Laimer full-backs, Danso, Affengruber or Bacher, Baumgartner and Schmid behind Gregoritsch. Predicted XIs disagree and some include players reported injured. Ireland predicted 3-4-2-1: Kelleher; Collins/O'Shea/Egan or Scales; Moylan, Idah, Parrott up front. Hallgrimsson: 'We'll see tomorrow'.
checks.rotation: Austria top the group and are unbeaten in 14 home games (11W, 3D); their last home defeat was 3-2 to Belgium in 2023. Ireland play Kosovo at the Aviva on Tuesday, after this game; no rotation signal from either side in the sources read. No confirmed rotation.
checks.motivation: Group B3: Austria lead with 8 points, unbeaten; a win secures promotion to League A. Ireland are third on 5 points after 4 games and need a result; two wins would put them top on head-to-head record (RTE). Both sides have a lot to play for; not a derby.
checks.form: Austria: unbeaten in last 4 (W,W,D,D in Nations League), no clean sheet in last 8 matches, five straight home wins (Racing Post). Ireland: L,W,D,D in Nations League, W,D,L,W,D,D across competitions, only defeat 1-0 to Kosovo; only away win in four came vs Israel on neutral ground. xG not found.
checks.h2h: Ireland 2-2 Austria in Dublin on 1 Oct 2026 (Ireland led 2-0 at half-time via Parrott goals, Prass and Gregoritsch equalised). Ireland unbeaten in last three meetings (one win). Austria leaky (no clean sheets in 8) and Ireland score; draw risk is real.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (data.odds): home 1.56, draw 4.00, away 5.25, de-vigged 59.3/23.1/17.6, opening 1.56/3.85/5.00. Paddy Power: Austria 4-7, draw 14-5, Ireland 4-1 (Racing Post); another preview lists 11/20, 3/1, 9/2. Polymarket 24h: Austria 0.615 to 0.605 (-1.6%, history from clob prices-history flat 0.615 then 0.605). Sources agree with market of 60/23/16.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating obtained: data.rating absent in the candidates file and the eloratings.net page fetched returned only historical rows, not the current rating. Only tipster predictions: Sports Mole 2-2, one tipster expects a draw. Model check is a gap.
checks.venue_weather: Raiffeisen Arena, Linz, Austria's home ground in a home fixture, kickoff 19:45, RTE2 broadcast. Dry and clear, about 7C by day dropping close to 0C by kickoff (RTE); no pitch issue reported. RTE's text mentions Sunday once in the weather note; other sources all say Saturday 14 Nov.

games.reason: Market has Austria 60.3% with draw 23.3%. Austria are a strong home side (14 unbeaten at home) but are missing several regulars (Wimmer, X. Schlager, Prass, Alaba, Wanner, Wober), have kept no clean sheet in 8, and drew 2-2 with Ireland in October after trailing 2-0. Ireland have little to lose and a low-risk 3-4-2-1 with Parrott in form. I shade the draw up by 2.7 points to 26% and Austria down 2.8 points to 57.5%, the away side stays near market. A straight home win is not allowed with a draw above 25%, so double chance or draw no bet is the better route. Confidence medium, not high, because lineups are unknown, the Austria injury lists conflict, and no Elo rating was found.
games.main_risk: Draw: Ireland's 2-2 in the first meeting, Austria's weakened midfield and attack with leaky defence (no clean sheet in 8) and Sports Mole's 2-2 prediction. Secondary risk: Austria XI uncertainty (Prass and X. Schlager fitness conflicting).
